regime: Mid-2026 presents a genuinely SPLIT macro regime — a stalled monetary-easing inflection sitting atop a wide-open credit and risk-appetite window — and the tension between the two is the defining feature of the tape. On the policy side, the Fed is "paused at the doorway": the funds target sits at 3.50-3.75% (effective 3.62%), already PAST the first turn lower (three cuts in late 2025) but plateaued at the April 28-29 FOMC after an Iran-war oil shock re-accelerated inflation — CPI +3.8% YoY (energy +17.9%), core PCE +3.3% (a 3-year high). That print froze the cutting path: the meeting produced the most dissents since 1992 (8-4, one dovish + three hawkish), and markets have repriced toward essentially NO further cuts in 2026, with June a near-certain hold. QT formally ended Dec 1, 2025 ($6.71T balance sheet), yet net liquidity is mildly TIGHTENING at the margin (~$5.80T, -5.3% YoY; reserves ~$3.01T) as TGA rebuild and currency growth drain reserves faster than the sheet re-grows, while elevated positive real yields (10y TIPS ~2.11-2.17%) act as a duration headwind. So the directional easing impulse that historically fuels small-cap/long-duration risk is PRESENT but STALLED — a tailwind on pause, not a green light. BUT the credit-and-positioning lens overrides any fear that financing is the binding constraint: credit is priced for perfection (IG OAS ~77bp, bottom decile; HY OAS ~272-275bp, near the June-2007 record low) with record speculative-grade issuance reaching low-quality borrowers, dormant volatility (VIX ~15.4), and a reopening IPO window (Q1-2026 proceeds strongest in 5 years, +78% YoY). Most decisively for this book, the small-cap signal is unambiguous: Russell 2000 +17.7-18% YTD vs S&P 500 +9.9%, record highs, longest win streak over the S&P since 1996, broadest breadth in a generation (~70% above 200-DMA, $45B+ ETF inflows), and a clean factor rotation OUT of mega-cap growth INTO small-cap/value/cyclicals (Energy/Materials/Industrials). The reconciliation: liquidity is on pause but capital availability and risk appetite are abundant — financing is NOT the constraint right now. The live caveats (a USD firming to ~100 on strong May payrolls reviving hike-talk; thin small-cap fundamentals with ~40% of R2000 earning nothing and a ~$368B maturity wall) are risks to monitor downstream, not reasons to narrow the hunt here.
posture: This regime OPENS the window for early-innings, capital-hungry small-cap theme hunting — exactly the waves this book wants. The credit/positioning lens dominates the practical read: financing is abundant (record HY issuance, tightest spreads since 2007, reopening IPO window), risk appetite is unconstrained (VIX dormant), and capital is actively rotating INTO small-caps, value and cyclicals — so themes with a genuine rising-capital demand mechanism can get funded and re-rated. Capex-funded bottlenecks (Energy/Materials/Industrials leadership signals where cyclical capital is flowing) and secular-growth early-innings themes are both favored. The one nuance from the rates lens: with the easing impulse stalled, draining reserves, and elevated real yields, the very longest-duration / most speculative-no-cash-flow corners face a marginal headwind versus quality-cash-generative names — so downstream tiers may want to caveat (not exclude) the most fragile balance sheets given the R2000 maturity wall. CRITICAL: this posture INFORMS theme selection, it does NOT gate it. In recall mode we surface wide; a stalled inflection or thin small-cap fundamentals are caveats to carry forward, never reasons to drop a candidate theme at Tier 0. A confirmed easing turn (cooler CPI/PCE + an actual cut + a dovish June 16-17 SEP/dot shift) would upgrade this from green-light-on-appetite to green-light-on-everything for aggressive multibagger risk-taking.

easing_inflection.basis: The two lenses reconcile to NEAR/STALLED. The rates lens is explicit: policy is PAST the first turn (three cuts in late 2025, formal easing lean with Gov. Miran dissenting FOR a cut) but the inflection STALLED when an Iran-war oil shock re-accelerated inflation (CPI +3.8% YoY, core PCE +3.3% 3-yr high), producing an 8-4 meeting (most dissents since 1992) and repricing the path toward ~no further 2026 cuts with June a near-certain hold — 'paused at the doorway,' a WATCH not a confirmed turn. The credit/risk lens does NOT contradict this on policy — it agrees the next Fed move is now ambiguous (strong May payrolls + USD back to ~100 revived hike-talk) — but shows that risk assets are behaving as if easing is effectively underway via abundant financing and record small-cap leadership. So: the monetary inflection itself is NEAR/stalled and unconfirmed, even as credit conditions already deliver an easing-like backdrop. Confirmation requires cooler May CPI (Jun 10) and a dovish June 16-17 FOMC SEP/dot plot plus an actual cut; a hawkish dot shift would flip the watch back toward 'no.'

The one tightening nuance from the rates lens is now louder: with 10y at 4.54%, real yields positive, reserves draining, and ~70% hike-by-EOY odds, the most fragile/speculative balance sheets face a real marginal headwind — caveat (never exclude) the weakest survival profiles and lean the asymmetry bar toward names with a visible cash/margin inflection. CRITICAL: this INFORMS theme timing, it does NOT gate. In recall mode 0b surfaces wide — a hawkish-tilted inflection, a one-day AI tremor, and thin small-cap fundamentals are all caveats to carry forward, never reasons to drop a candidate theme. regime: ENERGY-SHOCK REFLATION + HAWKISH HOLD WITH LIVE HIKE RISK, over a still-open financing window. Three facets converge on one read: (1) Monetary policy has flipped decisively hawkish — Iran-war oil shock (Brent ~$97, peaked ~$120-126 on blocked Hormuz) reaccelerated inflation (April headline CPI +3.8% YoY, core +2.8%, core PCE +3.3%); the May 5/Jun-5 jobs beat (+172K vs ~80-88K consensus, unemployment 4.3%) erased the cut narrative and made a 2026 HIKE the live tail (~70% by year-end on FedWatch, ~43% for a quarter-point by Dec). Warsh's first FOMC (Jun 17) is expected to drop the easing bias / erase the last 2026 cut dot or scrap the dot plot. (2) Risk/positioning: Jun 5 was a dual-driver risk-off (AI-valuation reset on Broadcom's held AI guide + good-news-is-bad-news jobs print) — Nasdaq Comp -4.18% (worst day since Apr 2025), Russell 2000 -3.47% (fell MORE than large-cap), VIX >20 (+~34-40%) but NOT panic; the H1 small-cap "great rotation" is fading, not confirming, and small-caps did NOT act as a defensive haven under a rate shock. (3) Liquidity/credit: the financing channel is wide open — HY OAS ~2.72% near the record-tight 2.41% low, IG ~77-80bp bottom-decile, IPO/HY/loan windows oversubscribed — but with first plumbing amber lights (reserves near the ~$2.8tn ample floor, SRF usage rebuilding, repo intermittently > SRF). CONFLICT RESOLVED: the regime is OPEN WINDOW over a HOSTILE TIDE — capital can still reach small-caps (spreads/issuance permissive), but the macro tide (rising real yields ~2.17% 10y TIPS, 10y ~4.5%+, hike risk) now actively derates long-duration, pre-profit small-caps rather than lifting them. Credit calm + equity-vol/rate repricing means this is a rate/valuation event, NOT a credit-stress or recession scare.
posture: SELECTIVE RISK-ON with demand-mechanism rigor — NOT broad small-cap beta. The open financing window justifies full theme exposure (pre-revenue names can still raise/refi/extend runway), but the hawkish reflation tide means the regime no longer subsidizes cash-burners, so lean HARD on the Tier-0 discriminating signals (converting backlog/RPO, dated binary milestone hit, firm fixed-price CASH anchor, visible GAAP-positive bridge) to separate real demand from issuance that is merely possible. OPENS: themes funded regardless of the Fed and benefiting from / insulated against the energy-geopolitical shock — energy services, oilfield/uranium/nat-gas infrastructure, grid & power bottlenecks, domestic supply-chain/defense (appropriated-funds demand), and self-funding cash-flow small-caps with firm converting backlog. CAUTIONS: pure rate-cut-dependent, long-duration speculative tech; rate-sensitive REIT/housing/biotech-burn; serial-dilution / B-/CCC refi-dependent names (the one cohort where the open window is softening); and any thesis leaning on a "Fed pivot" or a "broad rotation into small-caps" tailwind — both are being priced OUT, not in. Posture INFORMS selection; it does not gate the wide discovery pass.

easing_inflection.basis: The US is NOT at an easing inflection and has moved decisively the other way — a year-end 2026 HIKE is now the live tail (~70% by year-end, ~43% for a quarter-point by Dec on CME FedWatch), the lone remaining 2026 cut is expected to be erased from the dot plot at Warsh's Jun 17 FOMC (easing bias likely dropped or flipped to tightening), and the Apr 28-29 hold came on an 8-4 split (most dissents since Oct 1992). Driver: Iran-war oil shock (Brent ~$97, peaked ~$120-126) reaccelerated inflation (April CPI +3.8% headline / +2.8% core; core PCE +3.3% YoY, highest since May 2023), with Powell flagging the shock 'hasn't peaked yet.' Near-term binary regime events: May CPI Jun 10 (consensus ~3.9-4.0%, Cleveland Fed nowcast ~4.18%) and the Jun 17 Warsh FOMC+SEP. The only credible path back toward an easing inflection is oil/Hormuz de-escalation that lets headline inflation roll over — not a base case this week.
